entries.acceptance: Require all ancestry components unless an explicit permitted replacement is present; preserve the distinction from optional occupational suggestions.
Treat the baseline human ancestry as zero points and unspecified modifiers as zero; species, constructs and supernatural body types use the same package accounting.
Apply ancestry attribute deltas to personal attributes, derive secondary characteristics from those totals, and then apply personal and ancestry secondary adjustments exactly once.

A personal strength of 11 with +2 purchased health capacity, followed by ancestry strength +6 and health capacity +4, produces strength 17 and health capacity 23 without another charge for ancestry modifiers.
Personal dexterity 12 and health 12, ancestry dexterity +2 and health +1, personal speed +1, and ancestry speed -0.75 produce final speed 7.00; the personal speed purchase costs 20.
Compose occupational requirements and ancestry deltas with explicit origin tracking; removing an occupational suggestion cannot remove a mandatory ancestry component.
Combine compatible ancestry packages and add leveled ancestry modifiers; strength -1 and +6 combine to +5, with cost recomputed from the resolved components.
Require an authored conflict resolution identifying retained and removed traits and the resulting price; never infer that opposing ancestry traits cancel.
An approved omission of a positive ancestry trait retains the original ancestry price and records an equal negative personal replacement; that replacement counts against the personal negative cap.
An approved omission of a negative ancestry trait retains the original ancestry price and adds an equal positive personal replacement.
Allow supported modifiers on a replacement trait and calculate its actual cost and functional consequences; partial removal must not erase the entire underlying trait.
Exclude ancestry negative components and a negative ancestry package total from the personal negative cap without exempting unrelated personal negatives.
Keep ancestry quirks distinct from personal quirks and exclude them from the normal five-personal-quirk limit.
Represent species size with its size modifier, not individual build traits; an individual build adjustment remains relative to that ancestry and can change the final size modifier.
Store cosmetic and other zero-cost features without inventing prices; distinguish a baseline environmental adaptation from broader environmental tolerance.
Reject purchased attributes, traits and skills forbidden by an ancestry taboo, including later advancement and template composition, even though the taboo itself costs zero.
entries.validation_note: Owned zero-cost prohibitions validate trait IDs, purchased skill definitions and inclusive basic-attribute ranges. Shared learning and ordinary development offers gate prohibited purchases. Secondary ranges, ancestry composition and other purchase adapters remain pending; assertions authored and unrun.

entries.acceptance: Expose authored native gravity, atmosphere and temperature range to environmental assessment without granting tolerance beyond the declared baseline.
A single-skill ancestry bonus costs 2 per +1 up to +3, applies to its specialties and defaults, and does not itself grant training.
A single-skill ancestry incompetence costs -1 for -4, uses the ordinary incompetence restrictions, and is limited to five qualifying important skills.
Price each +1 to a related group at 5 for up to six skills, 10 for seven through twelve, and 15 for thirteen or more; cap the bonus at +4 and specify the group membership.
Price group incompetence with the corresponding negative talent cost and allow only one such group; apply it to all specialties of its member skills.
Compute training and improvement costs without ancestry skill bonuses or penalties, then apply those modifiers to the final score; bonuses do not purchase investment levels.
Price innate training by ordinary skill investment, display its relative level against ancestry-average attributes, and resolve actual level using each individual's attributes.
Treat innate and later personal training as one investment history; improving an average innate skill from attribute to attribute+1 costs two additional points.
A magical ancestry ability requires mana; apply the -10% mana-sensitive limitation only when no-mana regions are common in the campaign, with actual suppression in those regions.
Purchase innate spells as ancestry-learned skills while exempting their ordinary learning prerequisites; this exemption must not leak to unrelated learned spells.
Add ancestry spellcasting talent to innate spell skill; without that talent innate spells work only in high or very-high mana.
The base spellcasting talent costs five points even for innate-only casting; higher levels may carry the innate-only -40% accessibility limitation.
Apply ancestry subtypes as declared lenses with changed components and matching price differences, preserving mandatory inherited traits unless explicitly replaced.
A combined trait package exposes all component effects while charging their total once; use in ancestry and personal exotic abilities must share the same component identities.
A permitted bundle variant specifies changed components and reprices them; optional commonly associated traits are not granted by selecting the base bundle.
Switchable elemental forms use the alternate-form trait and the relevant package as its alternate ancestry; an ordinary package purchase must not grant free shape-changing.
Declare the base templates accepted by each lens, mutually exclusive lenses, and resolutions for repeated or conflicting components; reject unresolved combinations before commitment.
Add a resolved lens cost once and expose its components; the 101-point warrior plus -9 and +3 lenses totals 95.
For an equal-cost choice group, validate exactly the required number of distinct qualifying selections and their costs after variable-level adjustments.
For a point-pool choice, enforce both the allowed candidate set and required total; resolve self-control multipliers and variable-priced traits before testing the total.

Optimization may replace actual attribute, talent and skill investments, but cannot grant an additional price discount; six average skills reduced from relative +2 to +1 free 24 points, and raising dexterity consumes 20.
Present each skill's difficulty, relative level, investment and final score so derived totals remain inspectable after customization.
Author decisions specify player/nonplayer eligibility and campaign availability of each package; those permissions must be checked separately from whether its point total is affordable.

An ancestry definition may grant specifically authorized exotic, supernatural or ancestry-only traits; validation still rejects campaign-forbidden combinations and use outside required ancestry contexts.
Player-authored ancestry packages use the same structural and point validation as supplied packages plus an explicit campaign permission with a reason when rejected.
Keep recommended design ranges, suggested skill competence and the 90% starting-budget guideline as author guidance, not universal hard rejection thresholds.
An occupational package may reference a job's prerequisites, roll, pay and wealth level; selecting the package alone neither assigns employment nor pays wages.
Price an ancestry strength change of 1 at 10 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry dexterity change of 1 at 20 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry intelligence change of 1 at 20 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry health change of 1 at 10 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry health-capacity change of 1 at 2 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry fatigue-capacity change of 1 at 3 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry speed change of 0.25 at 5 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry will change of 1 at 5 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry perception change of 1 at 5 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.
Price an ancestry move change of 1 at 5 points with the same sign as the change, before applicable trait modifiers; retain ancestry origin in accounting.

Preserve distinct candidates, specialties and self-control pricing.

Resolve the supplied 100-point package from independently priced components. Resolve its 20-point positive and -35-point negative pools, two four-point primary skills, separate two-point combat and mobility choices, fixed one-point first aid and two one-point background choices.

Resolve the supplied 95-point package from independently priced components. Reproduce the component totals 100 attributes, 20 positive traits, -55 negative traits and 30 skills; skill results must change with later attributes without rebuying the template.

Resolve the supplied 35-point package from independently priced components. Validate attribute deltas, hearing and smell, fall protection, natural weapons, reflexes, armor, temperature tolerance, impulsiveness and sleep requirement; cosmetic tail and voice carry no extra points.

Validate all listed attributes, alternate bodies, feeding and environmental dependencies, regeneration restrictions, sunlight injury and permitted animal speech; the more durable optional variant costs 100 more and must replace its corresponding trait.

Independently sum the listed components to 261 points and execute their combined effects. Apply no breathing, food or sleep, metabolic immunity, agelessness, usually-active intangibility able to affect physical targets and usually-active invisibility against physical observers; visibility and tangibility changes inherit their component costs.

Independently sum the listed components to 171 points and execute their combined effects. Apply the same sustenance and aging exemptions but always-active intangibility and physical-observer invisibility; disallow becoming tangible, visible or affecting physical targets through supernatural powers.
Track the eight-hour mechanical reserve and three refuelings per day on the shared time/resource ledger; explicitly configured consumption traits can modify this baseline.
Mechanical bodies have no fatigue points to spend; action assessment must route machine exertion through its applicable rules rather than create a second fatigue balance.
Mechanical bodies undergo wear instead of biological aging; use the corresponding aging effects without incorrectly granting unlimited service life.
Mechanical bodies recover lost health only through applicable mechanical or electronic repair, unless an explicit trait changes that restriction.

exclusions.reason: Exclude setting descriptions, character names, illustrations, fiction and source wording. Retain the mechanical sample packages and worked arithmetic as neutral acceptance obligations.
Narrative design and worldbuilding advice has no mandatory numerical procedure. Guidance affecting permissions or validation is explicitly inventoried rather than converted into hard rules.
